quote: said Richard Wells, Managing Director of Insight Venture Partners, Anaqua's current controlling stakeholder.
status_event: Astorg bought the majority from Insight and Bessemer in 2019; Nordic Capital bought control from Astorg (announced November 2024, reported done February 2025).
notes: Only one Insight transaction is on record (July 2013). The firm's 2013 post says: "The terms of the agreement, which include the buyout of Anaqua’s existing investors, were not disclosed." (https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/anaqua-receives-major-growth-equity-investment-from-insight-venture-partners/). Bessemer invested beside Insight in 2013 (https://www.bvp.com/news/anaqua-acquisition-astorg). Astorg 2019: "Astorg has entered into an agreement to acquire the majority of shares in Anaqua from funds under the management of Insight Venture Partners and Bessemer Venture Partners." (https://www.astorg.com/news/astorg-to-acquire-anaqua-from-insight-venture-partners-and-bessemer-venture-partners). Form D of Anaqua Holding Corp (Delaware, incorporated 2013, filed 2015): issuer address is 745 Boylston Street, Boston, NOT Insight's address, so it is not a strict formd_vehicle; but four of five related persons are c/o Insight Venture Partners, 1114 Avenue of the Americas, with Blair Flicker, Mark Lessing, Peter Sobiloff and Euan Menzies as executive officers, and the box for a business combination is ticked. The quote states control at the 2019 sale; control at entry is inferred from the single 2013 transaction.

quote: an affiliate of private equity firm, Veritas Capital, will acquire the company from private equity and venture capital firm, Insight Venture Partners.
status_event: Veritas Capital bought BeyondTrust from Insight in 2014 for $310M; Bomgar bought it in 2018 and took the BeyondTrust name.
notes: No source found for the December 2006 entry into Symark itself; no earlier minority round by Insight is on record either. The verdict rests on the 2014 sale, where Insight is the named seller. Price from ZDNet (https://www.zdnet.com/article/veritas-capital-snaps-up-security-firm-beyondtrust-for-310-million/). HQ: the 2014 release is datelined Phoenix, AZ; Wikipedia gives Atlanta, Georgia for today's BeyondTrust (the former Bomgar). Wayback was not used: the machine-wide IA cooldown was active.

quote: Genstar Capital, the Company's current lead investor, will retain a significant minority investment going forward. Current minority investor Providence Equity will exit as part of this investment.
status_event: Spun Ministry Brands out to Reverence Capital in 2021; communitybrands.com now redirects to Momentive Software (checked 2026-09-26).
notes: The December 2016 entry is the Ministry Brands deal (announced 2016-10-31): the previous lead investor kept a minority and the other investor left, so Insight took the majority. Community Brands itself was formed in 2017 by combining YourMembership, Abila and Aptify; the firm's post calls Insight "the primary investor in Community Brands". NonProfit Times 2019: "Technology-based private equity firm Accel-KKR sold a majority stake in Abila software to Insight in April 2017" and "Another venture firm, Genstar Capital, kept a minority stake." (https://thenonprofittimes.com/news/shake-up-at-community-brands/). Same article: Insight "reportedly invested more than $1 billion in Ministry Brands" (an amount invested, not a priced valuation). WSJ article not readable (401).

quote: Harris Williams advised Digital Room Inc., a portfolio company of Insight Venture Partners, on its sale to H.I.G. Capital.
status_event: H.I.G. Capital acquired Digital Room in December 2017; Sycamore Partners bought it from H.I.G. in December 2021.
notes: Nothing found on the November 2002 entry itself. The evidence is the 2017 sale of the whole company, where the seller's adviser names Insight as the only sponsor; this is weaker than an explicit 'acquired from Insight', hence low. Insight's own team page says Adam Berger was Chairman and CEO of Digital Room, "an Insight portfolio company sold in 2017" (https://www.insightpartners.com/team/adam-berger/). H.I.G.: "H.I.G. acquired Digital Room in December 2017 in partnership with the Company’s senior management." (https://hig.com/news/h-i-g-capital-completes-the-sale-of-digital-room/). HQ: Insight's page says Van Nuys, H.I.G. in 2021 says Sherman Oaks (both Los Angeles). citybiz returned 403. Wayback not used (IA cooldown active).

quote: it has entered into a definitive agreement through which it will receive a majority investment from funds managed by global investment firm Carlyle (NASDAQ: CG) and global software investor Insight Partners.
status_event: Majority investment by Carlyle and Insight announced December 2023; still private, JMI Equity named as a further investor in September 2026.
notes: Control by a co-investor group (Carlyle and Insight); management, founders and Carrick Capital reinvested. 2023-12 is the announcement month; the closing date was not checked. Valuation: Alternatives Watch, 2023-12-19: "The valuation of the stake was not disclosed, but The Wall Street Journal pegged it at about $1.2 billion, according to unnamed sources familiar with the deal." (https://www.alternativeswatch.com/2023/12/19/carlyle-insight-partners-acquire-majority-stake-in-saas-provider-exiger/). That figure is sourced to unnamed people, not to the company. WSJ itself not read (paywall).

quote: TA, which first invested in GT in 2015, remains the company’s largest shareholder; Insight Partners and Cove Hill, an investor since 2018, will each be significant minority shareholders.
status_event: Strategic investment by Insight announced February 2022; TA Associates remained the largest shareholder.
sources_checked: company release 2022-02-09 on gtisoft.com (Business Wire copy returned 403)
notes: The company is owned by private equity firms (TA, Cove Hill, Insight), but Insight's own entry was a minority stake beside the existing owners. No valuation disclosed. The judge's note on the pre-filled $2.1B (belongs to Gamma, the presentation company) was not re-checked.

quote: Following the completion of the deal, Insight Partners will become the controlling shareholder of Incredibuild.
status_event: Raised a $35M Series B led by Hiro Capital in June 2022 at a reported $400M valuation; still private.
notes: The company's release does not say majority: it calls the $140M an investment with "both primary and secondary components" and says Insight "is joining Fortissimo Capital who acquired Incredibuild in 2018". Calcalist states control outright, and Globes 2022 agrees in substance: Insight is "the biggest investor in the company" and paid "most of the sum for buying Fortissimo's stake" (https://en.globes.co.il/en/article-software-co-incredibuild-raises-35m-doubles-valuation-1001416348). Globes dates the $140M to August 2021, which conflicts with the March 2021 release. Reported valuations are $200M (2021) and $400M (2022), both under $1B.

quote: But he confirmed that Insight took a majority investment, and that this funding comes on the heels of a lot of demand from financial and strategic investors to back the company.
status_event: Insight took a majority in January 2021; no later sale found in news through September 2026.
notes: 'He' is CEO Florian Winterstein. The same article says the round was "led by Insight Partners, with Iris Capital, eCAPITAL and Wecken & Cie. (all previous backers) also participating", which does not match the judge's note that those three were bought out; I found no source for a full buyout. The pre-filled status 'acquired' looks wrong: no acquisition of Jedox turned up. Valuation not disclosed.

quote: today announced it has closed a €130 million minority investment by Insight Partners, a leading global venture capital and private equity firm.
status_event: Bridgepoint agreed in July 2026 to buy a majority; Insight is to exit, closing expected by the end of 2026.
notes: CONTRADICTION WITH THE JUDGE'S NOTE: the note says the deal was reported in Belgium as a majority. I could not read any Belgian report saying so (De Tijd is paywalled). The company's own release says minority and adds that Insight "will join existing investor Dovesco, which acquired the business in 2018". De Rijkste Belgen says Insight paid 130 million euro for "een participatie in Netco, de Dovesco-holding boven Lansweeper" (https://derijkstebelgen.be/nieuws/nieuw-familie-jan-de-clerck-plaatst-314-miljoen-euro-bij-diversificatie-dochter). Exit: Built In, "Insight Partners and Imker Group will exit" (https://builtin.com/articles/bridgepoint-lansweeper-majority-stake-acquisition-20260729). ITdaily reports De Tijd heard a price of about 800 million euro, unconfirmed and under $1B. Release dateline is Grembergen, part of Dendermonde.

quote: New York-based software investor Insight Partners has acquired a majority shareholding in OptoScale, a Trondheim-based provider of underwater monitoring technology for the aquaculture industry.
status_event: Insight acquired a majority in May 2025; OptoScale bought Optimeering Aqua in August 2025.
notes: Terms not disclosed. Before the deal the largest shareholder was the Trondheim investment firm Cofounder (same article). The 2021 round of $4.1M (AgFunderNews headline) did not involve Insight as far as the headlines show; article not read.

quote: Insight Venture Partners joins Genstar and TA Associates, who will both retain minority stakes in PDI.
status_event: Bloomberg reported in March 2025 that Insight was weighing a sale of PDI at $4.5B or more; no sale found.
notes: No source read says 'majority' in so many words. The inference: both previous owners kept minority stakes, so the new investor holds the largest and presumably controlling stake. Supporting: the Bloomberg headline "Insight Said to Mull $4.5 Billion-Plus Sale of PDI Technologies" reads as the owner's sale (body not readable); the Form D of PDS Parent, Inc. (incorporated 2019, issuer address Alpharetta, not Insight's) lists three Insight directors (Parekh, Agarwal, Berger) against one each for Genstar and TA, out of seven. The $4.5B is a reported asking level, not a priced event.

quote: announced today it has closed a $60 Million Series C round led by private equity and venture capital firm Insight Venture Partners.
notes: The release names a round, not a purchase of control. The 2019 Form D of Prevalent, Inc. lists two Insight directors (Triplett, Krane) among seven directors, with both founders (Dambrot, Menz) still on the board, which fits a minority. Medium rather than high because $60M is large for the company's size at the time and no source states the stake; nothing read says majority. The firm's 2025 post says "in 2024, Miratech acquired Prevalent" (its spelling); the Mitratech release itself was not found. News results for 'Prevalent' are mostly noise (the common word).

quote: Insight Partners has been Thycotic’s majority owner since July 2015
status_event: TPG Capital bought Thycotic in 2021 for $1.4B and merged it with Centrify; the company was renamed Delinea in 2022.
notes: The 2015 release only says "a significant investment" with terms undisclosed; the majority is stated by CRN and by SiliconANGLE: "Thycotic is being purchased by TPG from majority owner Insight Partners" (https://siliconangle.com/2021/03/02/tpg-capital-enter-agreement-acquire-cybersecurity-firm-thycotic-1-4b/). Panel dates the entry June 2015, the release is dated 1 July 2015. Priced at $1B or more: $1.4B sale to TPG, reported 2021-03-02 (CRN headline says 'Report'). The Form Ds of Thycotic Software, LLC are option-plan filings from the company's Washington address, not an acquisition vehicle.

status_event: Acquired by Roper Technologies in 2020 for $5.35B.
sources_checked: EDGAR full-text search (2001 on, zero hits)
notes: A control transaction happened at the entry date, but no source read names Insight as one of the buyers. CNA 10-Q: "On November 30, 1999, CNA sold the majority of its interest in AMS Services, Inc. (AMS), a software development company serving the insurance agency market." CNA went from 89% to 9% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/000110465900000226/0001104659-00-000226.txt). CNA 10-K: the stake went "to a private management partnership" (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/21175/0000021175-00-000021.txt). At the 2004 sale the named sellers were not Insight: "Hellman & Friedman will acquire Windsor, Conn.-based Vertafore from Trident II and the MMC Capital Technology Fund, which are managed by MMC Capital Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Marsh & McLennan Companies Inc. and other minority investors." (https://www.propertycasualty360.com/2004/11/10/vertafore-ams-owner-sold-to-private-equity-firm/). So Insight was most likely a minority co-investor inside a buyout group led by MMC Capital. Under the rule that a purchase together with a co-investor group is control, this leans control, but only if Insight took part in the November 1999 purchase, which I could not establish. Wayback not used (IA cooldown active). Later priced events, all after Insight's exit: TPG $1.4B (2010, per Wikipedia's TPG page), Roper $5.35B (2020, Business Journals headline; article returned 403).
